text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:.
Business:
ADEVARUL
- SNCFR railway authority plans to increase tariffs by up to 200 percent.
- French businessmen plan to invest in Romania, the paper says.
- Shortage of funds affect start of spring farm works, the paper says.
- Copper mine at Rosia Poeni might be closed due to its huge debts.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The Danube was polluted by spills of petroleum products coming from Bucharest companies.
- Prices for milk and diary products expected to rise.
- Renel RA electricity authority has to cash 169 billion lei from its bad debtors.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The government decided to turn Romania's 16 domestic airports into regies autonomes which would benefit from state subsidies, the paper says.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Opposition National Unity Party (PUNR) sacked its leader Gheorghe Funar and appointed former farm minister Valeriu Tabara as interim president.
- Newspaper gives full-page report on French president Jacques Chirac's visit to Bucharest last week.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Convicts in prisons across the country ceased one-week protests and will start talks with the Justice Ministry.
- Ethnic Hungarian bishop Laszlo Tokes asked for more rights for ethnic Hungarians, including the creation of autonomous ethnic Hungarian regions in Transylvania.
ADEVARUL
- The government raised to 50,000 lei the monthly child allowance.
- Romania's exiled King Michael will start a one-week visit on Friday after the government restored his citizenship.
- Former president Ion Iliescu criticised the government for failing to invite opposition politicians at ceremonies organsied during Chirac's visit to Bucharest.

- Miners's union in the Jiu Valley coal field decided to support financially their leader Miron Cosma, arrested over his role in the 1991 miners' riots which ousted Romania's first post-communist government.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Iliescu fears that King Michael might claim back his properties, following the recent government decision to return Michael the Romanian citizenship.
- Only seven percent of Romanians are in favour of restoring monarchy and they don't pose a threat to the republican constitution, Socialist Party leader Tudor Mohora is quoted as saying.
- King Michael will be able to return to Romania and settle here like any citizen, PUNR secretary general Ioan Gavra said. ($= 7,744 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
